title: 5/22 fallback deadline force-delivered an early-game pick while its lock check said wait and later lineup windows were pending
missing_evidence: bts-scheduler journal for 2026-05-22 13:20-14:20 ET (B1 journal_*_retained.txt): the 13:28 'should_lock=False' line, the 13:53 FALLBACK REFRESH / delivery lines and the restart that found the pick locked - the 5/28 memo quotes them (reported)

the 2026-05-22 root pick JSON and scheduler state (B1 data/picks): primary game 824679 at 14:20 ET with projected_lineup=false, double-down game 824922 at 19:15 ET with projected_lineup=true, post-restart confirmed sides
tier_reason: delivery/decision impact as reported: a pick (with a projected-lineup double-down) was delivered and locked for the day although the lock decision said wait, cutting off later confirmed-lineup windows

contract.text: When the fallback refresh's lock decision is should_lock=False and later scheduled lineup checks still have pending confirmations, the scheduler waits instead of force-delivering; it force-delivers only when no future pending window remains (never missing the submission window).

mechanism.text: at the fallback deadline run_day refreshed the pick (_refresh_pick_at_fallback) and delivered it unconditionally via _deliver_and_lock_pick; the refresh's should_lock result and whether later lineup windows were still pending were not consulted, and the deadline was driven by the early primary game
once delivered and locked, a scheduler restart short-circuited on the locked pick, so later lineup checks could not replace it

verified_recovered.how: 5/28 production exercised the defer path: fallback deferred at 13:43 ET (should_lock=False, future windows pending) and a later check delivered at 15:10 ET (reported in the 5/28 memo)

residual.text: Accepted tradeoff of the defer path: waiting can lead to a later, weaker or no pick; on 8/27-8/30 deferral abandoned enterable picks and one DM went out after cutoff (E84/I-084), fixed with the deadline-aware fallback on 8/30.
A projected double-down could still ride through on the primary's confirmation (gap rule alone) until the both-slots gate of 7/10 (audit F2: 11 production days, 4 locked 51-133 min early).

watchdog.trigger: a pick is delivered while its latest lock decision is should_lock=False and a later scheduled lineup check still has unconfirmed sides, outside the final no-future-window fallback
watchdog.recovery_assertion: the day's delivered pick either passed should_lock or was delivered by the final fallback with no pending future window, before cutoff

evidence.what: quoted scheduler behaviour: 13:20 ET lineup check with 28 teams still projected; 13:28 candidate should_lock=False (gap vs best projected below threshold); no scheduled check before the fallback deadline of the 14:20 ET primary game; 13:53 fallback refresh kept the same candidate; the scheduler force-delivered before first pitch; a restart soon after found the pick locked; the root pick JSON shows the double-down on a projected lineup
5/28: fallback deferred at 13:43 ET with should_lock=False and future windows pending; a 15:10 ET check locked with should_lock=True and delivered by DM

notes: prelim OI?; UC only on the evidence rule: the detailed account is the 5/28 memo (6 days later) quoting journal lines and the pick JSON (reported); 324c4a2 (5/23, within 48 h) has an empty body. The B1 journal (retained from 5/11) and pick files should make this observed_incident

arguably a decision-contract change rather than a code defect: the pre-fix fallback deliberately bypassed should_lock to avoid missing the window; 324c4a2 changed the contract to defer when later windows remain (hence secondary P)
